work.title: The Mathieu property for quadratic complements
work.abstract: For a nondegenerate quadratic form $q$ of dimension $N\geq 1$ over a characteristic-zero field, the kernel of the normalized rotation and scaling trace on $\{q\neq 0\}$ is Mathieu–Zhao exactly when $N\leq 2$. In every higher dimension a single witness attains the minimum pole order, numerator degree and polynomial multiplier degree, namely $(1,3,1)$. A second witness gives sharp degree cutoffs for its detecting multipliers. For an arbitrary regular phase, testing finitely many multipliers at one computable order decides eventual vanishing against every fixed multiplier. For phases affine in the angular variable, a Laurent support criterion suffices. Over $\mathbb{R}$, the kernel of the special orthogonal Reynolds projection is Mathieu–Zhao exactly when $q$ is definite or $N\leq 2$.
